title: Entry growth in Gaussian elimination
summary: Gaussian elimination is one of the oldest algorithms in mathematics, and the most popular method for solving an unstructured linear system. Its stability in finite precision is controlled by its growth factor, which measures how large the entries produced during elimination can become. Understanding the worst-case behavior of this quantity has been a central problem in numerical analysis since the 1940s.
